statement_summary: Maintain a documented security program
Owner designated security lead and incident commander
Annual risk assessment using SP 800-30
Risk decision rules; High risks never accepted as they are
Annual evaluation with periodic outside review
Client agreement security terms recorded and checked before signing
No agreement, no client data; client consent where required
Vendor list and annual SOC 2 review of the suite provider
Helper agreement and Client A approval before access
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Rev. 3A Table 9.3a third-party contractors via CSCA-A (9))

statement_summary: Gateway only from the standard account over the hotspot or business network; password only in the password manager
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Rev. 3A Table 9.3a remote and third-party connections via CSCA-A (3))

statement_summary: Gateway session log and weekly review answers
MFA on every service that offers it
Unique passphrases in a password manager; no browser-saved passwords
Standard daily account; administrator account for installs only
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Rev. 3A Table 9.3a approved use via CSCA-A (3))

statement_summary: Quarterly account review
Signing certificate on a hardware token with a PIN
Monthly review of the suite sign-in history
Sealed emergency access envelope with the owner's attorney
Four-level classification
Security-sensitive material read only in the portal or on site; never kept
Marking of derived notes and photos
CEII purpose and recipient limits; pre-release check on Client B deliverables
Encryption on every device and drive
Field photos moved the same day; no personal cloud sync
Weekly encrypted backup in the locked cabinet; quarterly restore test
No removable media on client equipment
Client information register; return or destroy with a certificate
Shredding and recorded device disposal
Business network or hotspot, never the household network
AI tools only after assessment, terms review, and client consent; never CEII; AI output never a conclusion
Annual training including information-stealing malware
Field rules: escort and photo rules; no personal-device photos by the field assistant
Incident runbook with printed contacts
24-hour client notices by phone then in writing
Report unauthorized CEII disclosure to FERC promptly
No ransom without legal advice and an OFAC check
Peer engineer arrangement and client call list
